title: Taifa of Alpuente
capsule: The Taifa of Alpuente was a small Muslim successor state in the Valencia region of al-Andalus, governed by the Berber Banu Qasim dynasty from c. 1010 following the disintegration of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba in the fitna (civil war). Centred on the mountain fortress of Alpuente north of Valencia, it was one of the smallest of the reyes de taifas kingdoms, surviving by navigating between the larger taifas of Valencia and Zaragoza. The Almoravid advance through al-Andalus ended the taifa period; Alpuente was absorbed around 1106–1111.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. As a minor taifa, Alpuente's territorial extent is inferred from later Aragonese conquest records and Arabic chronicles rather than precise contemporary surveys; boundaries are approximate.
